newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
DEMAND TO REVEAL ARMS SCAM BENEFICIARIES

Several political functionaries and legal experts demanded that names in the Bofors case bank documents be made public. However, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said it had no immediate plan to disclose the names of anyone connected to the $1.3 billion 155 mm Howitzer deal. Meanwhile, the CBI may send letters rogatory to several countries after completing scrutiny of the secret bank documents, sources said. They said the letters rogatory could be sent as the secret documents indicated that money was transferred from Swiss banks to banks in other countries.
Indian Express
CABINET EXPANSION LIKELY BY MID-FEBRUARY

Six or seven ministers, among them Ajit Singh and Saifuddin Soz, are likely to be inducted into the cabinet slated for expansion between February 9 and 12. This time the emphasis would be on members of the minority communities. The list of likely incumbents for cabinet posts include two women and three Moslem members of parliament.
The Pioneer
PARTNERS MAY FORCE CHOICE ON PREMIER

Even though the presidential election is six months away, a broad consensus appeared to be emerging within the ruling United Front (UF) over the candidature of Vice President K.R. Narayanan for the post. Although UF leaders and ministers maintained the issue was not on their agenda, privately they admitted that Narayanan would be the front-runner as a consensus candidate. Narayanan, being a former Congress leader, would be acceptable to the Congress party, whose support is vital for getting the nominee elected. The talk of Narayanan's candidature is a clear signal that there are few backers for President Shankar Dayal Sharma seeking another term.
The Economic Times
REVISED GUIDELINES FOR EXTERNAL BORROWINGS EXPECTED

The Finance Ministry is expected to issue revised guidelines for external commercial borrowings (ECBs) allowing major relaxations. The ministry is likely to relax ECB end-use norms to allow foreign loans to be used for project related rupee expenditure in case of roads, bridges, airports, ports, sanitation and sewerage, water supply and irrigation projects. So far, the concession on rupee expenditure was extended only to power, telecommunications and railways as per guidelines. Additionally, as a special case, companies supplying inputs to the infrastructure sector would also be allowed use of foreign loans for rupee expenditure on a case-by-case basis.
BUDGET TO WIDEN TAX BASE, CONTROL FISCAL DEFICIT

The forthcoming budget would contain measures to widen the tax base, enhance social sector expenditure and to control the fiscal deficit, the Finance Minister said. Indicating the budget may contain tax sops and other incentives to attract investors' funds into the infrastructure sector, he said there was a need for a sharper fiscal correction and pursuance of investor friendly policies particularly in the infrastructure sector. Out of the total non-plan expenditure of 1,500 billion rupees, 1,300 billion was committed expenditure, providing little flexibility for cuts, the minister said.
LAW TO PUT BANKS, FIS UNDER ONE ROOF MOOTED

The Finance Ministry is trying to introduce comprehensive legislation to cover the functioning of all banks. In a recent parliamentary committee meeting on this issue, the ministry reiterated that all banks should come under one law. However, all state owned banks have opposed the move. Banking sources said the issue was further complicated with some financial institutions (FIs) enquiring whether they qualified as banks. Sources said FIs such as Industrial Development Bank of India, Small Industries Development Bank of India and the Export Import Bank of India were promoted as banks for all legal purposes.
HIKE LIKELY IN UREA PRICES

A 10 percent hike in the price of urea is on the anvil. The Agriculture Ministry has already recommended a hike and the matter is likely to come up before the cabinet for a final decision. Although experts had recommended a 30 percent increase, the Agriculture Minister agreed to a 10 percent hike keeping in mind the political sensitivity of the issue with the farming community. The ministry is thinking of utilising the additional resources raised by the hike to subsidise other varieties of fertiliser. The proposed hike is aimed at correcting the lop-sided pattern of fertiliser consumption.
POLICY TO BOLSTER EXPORTS SOON

The Commerce Ministry has evolved a short and long-term policy to boost exports. The policy was sketched in the wake of a poor export performance in the previous year. The Commerce Minister said he had asked export promotion councils to put forward their problems which would be perused before evolving the policy. The minister, in recent talks with various export promotion councils, had assured them of his ministry's full support. He told exporters the government would try to incorporate their suggestions in the new policy and assured them of clearing bottlenecks to accelerate export growth.
Financial Express
IT INDUSTRY ON OVERDRIVE FOR BILL GATES' VISIT

The subcontinent is warming up to the first ever visit by Microsoft Corporation chief Bill Gates. Information technology companies are trying to get Gates to appear in their events, specially designed for the occasion. Microsoft India, in association with Compaq, Digital, the Living Media group and United Airlines is making a serious bid to rope in Gates. However, a host of other companies too have made similar requests.
Business Standard
BANK GUARANTEES OF TWO TELECOM FIRMS TO BE ENCASHED

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has sought to encash bank guarantees of two basic services companies - Essar Commvision and Usha group's TechnoTelecom. The decision was taken after the companies failed to furnish the financial and performance guarantees after accepting the letters of intent, DoT officials said. Essar had provided a 250 million rupee bank guarantee for the Punjab circle and Techno Telecom 150 million for Bihar. Company executives said they were examining legal options and it was likely they would move the courts. Basic Teleservices has already challenged a DoT move to encash its guarantees for Tamil Nadu.
PETRO GOODS PRICE INCREASE LIKELY AFTER MARCH 31

A consensus appears to be emerging among constituents of the ruling coalition on the need to increase prices of petroleum products to check the rising oil pool account deficit. The Left parties have, however, ruled out two price increases in one financial year. This indicated that the price hike can come about only after March 31, 1997. The government had increased petro goods' prices prior to the budget session of parliament in the previous year. A final decision on the issue is expected at the coalition's core group meeting on February 9, 1997.
TELECOM PACKAGE ON THE ANVIL

The government is set to announce a package of incentives to jump start plans to usher in private players into the state-controlled field of telecommunication services. Major concessions include a five-year tax holiday for the projects, possible treatment of licence fees as capital expenditure and raising limits on external commercial borrowings. The package is expected to be announced soon after getting clearance from the finance ministry and department of telecommunications.
The Observer
DIAMOND TRADERS WELCOME DE BEERS-RUSSIA PACT

The diamond industry has welcomed the informal exclusive marketing agreement between De Beers of London and the Russian government. This would end the year-long uncertainty concerning the fate of Russian roughs since the country's gems and jewellery sector primarily depended on roughs supplied by De Beers, sources said. Under the proposed agreement, De Beers would buy nearly 50 percent of the total production of Russian roughs against about 95 percent under the old agreement. Smuggling of Russian rough diamonds via Antwerp and other outlets would come to an end following the agreement, Gem and Jewellery Promotion Council sources said.
MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT PLUG FOR LOWER PERSONAL TAXES

Members of parliament (MPs) urged the Finance Minister to reduce income tax rates, rationalise customs and excise tariffs and eliminate double taxation on dividends in the forthcoming budget. The minister was also asked to impose presumptive taxes on consumption of luxury items and raise the exemption limit for small-scale industries. The MPs asked the minister to step up budgetary support for social sectors, while ensuring progressive reduction in fiscal deficit. Although the members were divided on the issue of a Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) levied on zero-tax companies, the MPs agreed on the need to do away with double tax on dividends. Business Line
OIL MAJORS DEFER PRIVATE PLACEMENT PLANS

Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum have deferred their proposed plans for private placement of debt to raise short-term funds. Bankers said the oil companies decided not to enter the market now offering a higher coupon, as there were clear indications of a softening of interest rates, especially at the short end of the market. Officials said the oil companies could always tap the Oil India Development Board for cheaper funds in the near-term rather than resort to costly market borrowings.
CALL MONEY RATES CRASH

Call money rates crashed to a low of 0.1 percent towards close on Tuesday. Hardly any deals were done in the inter-bank money market as most banks had covered the cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement for the fortnight, dealers said. Opening at 0.5 percent, overnight rates fell with lenders quoting as low as 0.1 percent. Rates plunged to the lowest level despite the series of Repo auctions by the central bank since the beginning of the month. Dealers, pointing out that offtake of credit was yet to pick up, felt the system had excess liquidity.
